sector_verification_note: TIER C BY NATURE, like Sector 1. Nothing in Indian general management is statutorily licensed — no council controls who may call themselves a marketer, an HR professional or a consultant. The one Tier B fact that governs the sector is CAT eligibility, and it is the most OPEN gate in the taxonomy: any three-year degree in any subject, 50 percent, no age limit, no attempt cap. That is why almost every record here is class12_prerequisite 'any' and mid_stream_entry 'after_any_degree'. This is the sector a student who took a wrong turn elsewhere can still reach.

nuances.statement: This record strains the profession test and is included deliberately. It earns its place as the destination those skills combine into, and because leaving it out would make the sector's own name false.

The only record in the taxonomy whose early_earnings band starts at zero, and that is not a formatting artefact. A founder can earn nothing for years. Every other profession here pays from the first month.

admin_review.reason: The economics are unlike anything else in the dataset: outcomes are extremely dispersed, survivorship bias is severe in every available source, and a range is close to meaningless. Decide whether to show numbers at all for this record, or present it with the range suppressed and the risk stated instead. Also decide whether it should surface for school-age users at all, or only for college and working-age ones.

routed_elsewhere.why: Object of concern is money and value, not the organisation and its customers.
Same boundary — capital and markets are Sector 6.
Delete company law and the role disappears entirely. Governance, not management. See DECISIONS.md section 2.1.
Hospitality management is its own sector, with its own object of concern — the guest.
Events belong with hospitality and experience, not general management.
Making the advertisement is a creative craft; deciding who to show it to is marketing.
Teaching-anything rule. L&D Specialist is retained here as a job role.

boundary_decisions_needing_your_signoff: ENTREPRENEUR is included despite failing half the profession test — the skill set is not separate, it is sales plus operations plus finance combined. Kept because the sector is named for it and because omitting it would make the taxonomy claim that entrepreneurship is not a career. Flagged high for its economics.

RETAIL & STORE OPERATIONS and LOGISTICS & WAREHOUSE OPERATOR are BASE-LAYER professions, added on the Mason-beside-Civil-Engineer precedent. They employ at enormous scale, they are formal organised-sector jobs with salary slips, and they are among the few formal entry-level jobs available in tier-2 and tier-3 cities. They are also removed by the formal_workplace_track preference preset — deliberately, since that filter is opt-in.
MANAGEMENT CONSULTANT versus IT BUSINESS & SYSTEMS ANALYST (Sector 1) scored a real overlap on probe. Kept separate on skill set: systems and SQL versus organisation and strategy. Contestable.
MARKET RESEARCH ANALYST versus STATISTICIAN (Sector 3) versus DATA ANALYST (Sector 1). Split by object of concern: the customer, inference itself, and the company's own operational data.

OPERATIONS & ADMINISTRATION MANAGER absorbed Hospital Administrator and the health records roles from Sector 4. That makes it a wide profession spanning a hospital administrator and a medical records officer. Confirm the merge is not too broad.

1.0: TIER C BY NATURE — nothing in Indian general management is licensed. The sector's only statutory fact is CAT eligibility, which is the most open gate in the taxonomy.

All six promises made to this sector were kept: Product Manager and Project Manager as professions; Digital Marketer and SEO Specialist into Marketing Specialist; Medical Representative into Sales Professional; Hospital Administrator and Health Information Technician into Operations & Administration Manager.

Added two BASE-LAYER professions the taxonomy was missing entirely — Retail & Store Operations and Logistics & Warehouse Operator. Between them they cover employment in the tens of millions, concentrated exactly where formal entry-level work is scarcest.

ECONOMICS ARE ALL 'judgment'. No Indian salary source was fetched for this sector, and after the Sector 4 finding that commercial aggregators disagree by four to five times on the same profession, unsourced figures are not marked verified. Recorded as a sector_admin_review.

Two exact-duplicate job roles renamed: 'Forklift Operator' also existed under Heavy Equipment Operator in Sector 2 (construction plant, not warehousing) and 'Product Analyst' under Data Analyst in Sector 1 (product ANALYTICS, not product management). Same string, different jobs.

sector_admin_review.reason: Every economics block in this sector is 'judgment' with no sources. The figures are reasoned from the Indian graduate market rather than fetched, and they must be sourced before the sector ships. Sales Professional and Entrepreneur are the two worst cases: sales pay is heavily variable and the fixed-pay view understates it, and entrepreneurship outcomes are so dispersed that a range may be the wrong format entirely.
